newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesia late palm olein stable, interest thin.
newsitem.headline: Indonesia late palm olein stable, interest thin.

text.p: Indonesian palm olein prices were mostly stable in late trading on Thursday, with buyers showing little interest amid a directionless Malaysian market.

Traders said palm olein was quoted at 1,350 rupiah/kg in Jakarta, unchanged from the opening, but trades were also heard at as low as 1,335 rupiah. There has been no crude palm oil tender so far this week in the wake of declines in palm olein.

"Buyers are holding out in anticipation of prices falling further," one trader said. "I think the market will see prices opening five rupiah lower tomorrow because I heard buyers were not keen on buying olein even at 1,335 rupiah today."
The traders said an extremely slow Malaysian market, with a total of just 500 lots done with 15 minutes left before the close, kept the local market stagnant as well.

"There were no fresh leads or direction coming from Malaysia, and this kept activity very thin," one trader said. "Buyers are not taking positions because of expectations that prices could go down some more."
The traders said, however, improving export margins were keeping exporters busy. "Exports have been increasing following an improvement in margins," one trader said.

Data from Belawan Port showed that the MT Acada-Dolphin will leave for India on Friday with 5,500 tonnes of palm olein. The MT Golden Gion will leave the North Sumatran port on Friday for Dumai with 7,000 tonnes of palm stearin.

The MT Sapphire will also leave on Friday for Tanjung Priok, Jakarta, with 1,200 tonnes of coconut oil, while the KM Pershing will leave for Tanjung Priok on Thursday with 4,600 tonnes of coconut oil.
